scope: Corollary A.4 (Three-cell smoothing) of the manuscript “Exponential PSD rank of positively shifted matching matrices” (preprints/Exponential-PSD-rank-of-positively-shifted-matching-matrices-October-5-2026/shifted-matching-psd.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 126 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7e90c5f1e508114d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed K > 0, there are an integer d ≥ 1 and N0 with the following property. Let N ≥ N0 be even, and let a, b, c be positive integers summing to N. For a uniform ordered partition into cells of these sizes, prescribe x, y, z edges between the first and second, first and third, and second and third cells, respectively. Assume that x, y, z are nonnegative integers and that a − x − y, b − x − z, c − y − z are nonnegative even integers. Let Tx,y,z average functions on perfect matchings subject to these counts, and let Πd project onto the edge-product span of degree at most d, using uniform measures as above. Then ∥Tx,y,z(I − Πd)∥op ≤ N−K uniformly in all the sizes and admissible triples. For every fixed partition and matching function f, the values Tx,y,zΠdf are given by one polynomial of total degree at most d in (x, y, z) across all admissible triples.
